comments.author: @samiamgreeneggs37
comments.text:
Hi John (@johnferrellesq):
Thanks for another excellent video.  
Request #1:  Please clarify to what extent multiple Utility Patents can be filed within a year of filing a single Provisional Patent application that clearly describes all of the features of the future multiple Utility Patent Claims, all originating 21 years of protection starting with the single original Provisional filing.  
In my case, I've submitted my first (thanks to you!) detailed Provisional Patent application featuring 29 drawing sheets and 23 specification pages thoroughly describing the function, uses, and materiality, as well as the methodology for developing the invention's geometry.  I believe that at least one feature has applications in multiple USPTO Classes.
Request #2:  One month after submitting the Provisional Patent application referred to above, I developed an additional feature, and plan to submit a second Provisional Patent application identical to the first, and with the new feature added.  Assuming that I submit one or more Utility Patents within a year of the first Provisional filing that clearly Claim the same features described in both Provisional applications, to what extent can I have 21 years of protection starting from the initial Provisional submittal date, while also having 20 years and 11 months of protection just for the added feature/Claim?
A thousand thank yous in advance,
-Sam I am
